blocks.text: The National Assembly can pass a law banning open grazing, but no cow moves unless somebody enforces it. Turning words in a statute book into action on a road in Benue is the work of the executive.

blocks.markdown: The **executive** is the organ of government that implements and enforces the law and carries out the day-to-day administration of the state. In Nigeria executive power is vested in the President by section 5 of the 1999 Constitution, and is exercised through the Vice-President, ministers, and the whole machinery of ministries, departments and agencies.

items: **Implementation of laws and policies** — the executive's defining function.
**Maintenance of law and order** — through the police and other security agencies.
**Defence and external relations** — commanding the armed forces, appointing ambassadors and negotiating treaties.
**Policy initiation** — preparing executive bills and the annual budget estimates for the legislature.
**Appointments** — nominating ministers, ambassadors, heads of agencies and, on the recommendation of the National Judicial Council, judges.
**Delegated legislation** — making rules, regulations and orders under powers granted by statute.
**Prerogative of mercy** — pardoning, commuting or remitting punishment.
**Provision of public services** — health, education, roads, water and electricity.

blocks.title: Political and permanent executive
blocks.text: The POLITICAL executive consists of the elected and politically appointed officeholders — President, Vice-President, ministers, commissioners — who set policy and leave when the government changes. The PERMANENT executive consists of career civil servants — permanent secretaries, directors and other officers — who advise on and implement policy and remain in office across administrations. Their permanence is what gives government continuity.

rows: Executive authority vested in one person
The President of Nigeria; the President of the United States
Executive authority vested in a committee or council of equals
Holds the title and performs formal duties but exercises no real power

blocks.markdown:
### Controls on executive power

Because the executive commands the police, the army and the treasury, it is the organ most capable of abuse. Nigeria's Constitution restrains it in several ways: legislative confirmation of senior appointments; the requirement that at least one minister be appointed from each state, a **federal character** provision in section 147; the need for an Appropriation Act before money may be spent; legislative oversight and investigation; impeachment for gross misconduct; judicial review of executive acts; enforceable fundamental rights; a two-term limit on the presidency; and, ultimately, periodic elections and a free press.

blocks.title: Sorting a day's actions into executive functions
blocks.prompt: In one week a President signs a treaty on cross-border trade, commutes a death sentence to life imprisonment, forwards budget estimates to the National Assembly, and issues regulations under an existing Act on fuel quality. Name the executive function exercised in each case.

steps.text: Signing the trade treaty is the conduct of external relations, exercised as Head of State; it will normally require legislative ratification to take effect domestically.
Commuting the death sentence is the exercise of the prerogative of mercy.
Forwarding budget estimates is policy initiation and the exercise of financial initiative; the legislature must still enact the Appropriation Act.
Issuing fuel quality regulations under an existing Act is delegated legislation — the executive making rules with legislative authority.
Note the pattern: two of the four actions require the legislature to complete them, which is checks and balances in operation.

blocks.answer: External relations; prerogative of mercy; policy initiation and financial initiative; delegated legislation

blocks.title: Executive is wider than President
blocks.text: Candidates often equate the executive with the President alone. Say clearly that the executive includes the political executive, the permanent civil service, the police and armed forces, and public corporations and agencies. That breadth earns extra marks in essay answers.

points: The executive implements and enforces laws and administers the state day to day.
Its functions include maintaining order, defence, external relations, policy initiation, appointments, delegated legislation and the prerogative of mercy.
The political executive is temporary and makes policy; the permanent executive is career civil service and implements it.
Executives may be single or plural, and nominal or real.

Nigeria vests executive power in the President under section 5 of the 1999 Constitution, restrained by legislative confirmation, appropriation, oversight, impeachment, judicial review and a two-term limit.

sources.title: Constitution of the Federal Republic of Nigeria 1999 (as amended), sections 5, 147 and 175
